title: Integrated Finance & Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition (2027 Q1)
author: Daniela Romero
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines the integrated operating model for Redwood Inference’s finance and legal controls spanning: annual and rolling budgeting & forecasting, contract lifecycle and legal review standards, procurement approvals and vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition (RevRec) and billing policies. The document is intended for finance, legal, procurement, product and engineering managers responsible for spend, contracts, and revenue compliance.

Goals:
- Ensure predictable budgeting and forecasting that aligns to product roadmaps and capacity commitments.
- Standardize contract review and signature workflows to minimize legal risk and accelerate sales/partner motion.
- Establish procurement thresholds, controls, and preferred vendor categories to control spend and support scaling.
- Provide RevRec and billing rules consistent with ASC 606 principles and Redwood’s SaaS/consumption billing model.

1) Scope and Ownership
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood entities for purchases, contracts, customer billing, and revenue accounting.
- Primary owners:
  - Finance: overall budgeting, forecasting, billing configuration, and revenue accounting.
  - Legal: contract templates, risk review, signature authority guidance.
  - Procurement (Finance team): vendor onboarding, PO issuance, and vendor payment controls.
  - Product/Engineering: provide workload forecasts and capacity commitments that feed budgeting.

2) Budgeting & Forecasting
Intro:
Redwood operates a hybrid budgeting model: annual budgeting for strategic planning and quarterly rolling forecasts for operational accuracy. Finance publishes the annual budget in November with a rolling 12-month forecast updated monthly.

Inputs and cadence:
- Annual Budget (published Nov 15): approved by CFO and CEO; includes headcount plan, committed Dedicated capacity deals, CAPEX requests for large hardware purchases, and GTM spend.
- Monthly Rolling Forecast (updated by 5th business day): reconciles bookings, usage trends (hosted API), Dedicated commitments, and pipeline-led revenue changes.
- Capacity Forecast (weekly): product/infra teams provide 12-week GPU capacity forecast for Dedicated pool planning.

Approval thresholds and owners (table):
| Item | Threshold | Approver | Finance Code/Comments |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Operating expense (non-headcount) | <= $25k | Finance manager | OP-XX | PO recommended for > $5k |
| Operating expense | $25k – $250k | Budget owner + Finance director | OP-YY | Business case required |
| Capital / hardware spend | > $250k | VP Finance + CFO | CAPEX-01 | Requires procurement + infra sign-off |
| Headcount | All hires | People Ops + Hiring manager | HC-01 | Headcount request form required |

Budget control & variance process:
1. Budget owners reconcile monthly expenses and submit variance explanations if monthly variance > 5% of line item or > $20k.
2. Finance aggregates variances and presents at monthly FP&A review.
3. Significant budget reallocation (> $100k) requires CFO approval and update to the rolling forecast.

3) Contracts & Legal Process
Purpose:
Standardize contract execution to reduce legal risk, ensure consistent revenue terms, and speed time-to-close.

Contract lifecycle summary:
1. Initiation: Sales/product/partnerships create an initial term sheet or MSA request in the contract intake form.
2. Commercial review: Revenue/Finance validates pricing, billing cadence, and recognition triggers.
3. Legal review: Legal performs risk assessment using the Contract Risk Matrix.
4. Negotiation: Track changes in the clause-by-clause redline and maintain a change log in the contract tracker.
5. Approval & signature: Use the approval matrix below.
6. Contract ingestion: Final executed agreement uploaded to contract repository (DocuSign + internal KMS link) and key terms logged in CRM + Finance system.

Contract Risk Matrix (examples):
- Low risk: standard SaaS MSA, no custom indemnities, standard data processing addendum.
- Medium risk: vendor contracts with indemnity caps > $500k, addendum with customer-specified SLAs, or custom data residency requests.
- High risk: government/customer with classified data, bespoke IP assignment, or cross-border export-control implications.

Approval & signature authority (table):
| Contract Value / Type | Pre-Approved Template? | Approver(s) | Signature Authority |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| <= $100k (standard MSA) | Yes | Sales manager + Finance director | Head of Sales (up to $100k) |
| $100k – $1M (non-standard) | No | Legal + Finance director + VP Sales | CEO delegated up to $1M |
| > $1M or High Risk | No | Legal + CFO + CEO | CEO + Board notification |

Key legal controls and checklists:
- Always use the current company MSA template unless Legal approves deviation.
- Data Processing Addendum (DPA) required if personal data is processed; attach approved DPA template.
- SLA credits: Finance must validate the operational and billing impact of any SLA credit language prior to acceptance.
- Confidentiality: mark contracts Confidential and store in secure contract repository.

4) Procurement Procedures and Vendor Onboarding
Procurement categories and preferred vendors:
- Cloud infrastructure (preferred: major public cloud providers)
- GPU hardware vendors (preferred: OEM partners with support contracts)
- SaaS tooling (IT approved list maintained quarterly)

Procurement approval flow (step-by-step):
1. Request: Requester submits procurement request in the procurement portal including business justification, vendor quotes, and proposed PO amount.
2. Procurement review: Procurement assesses vendor risk, preferred vendor status, and consolidates quotes.
3. Finance approval: Approves budget code and issues PO for approved purchases. For card purchases <= $5k, local card policy applies.
4. Legal review: If contract terms accompany purchase and exceed threshold or contain custom terms, route to Legal.
5. Vendor onboarding: Complete W-9/KYC, insurance verification, and security questionnaire for vendors with access to customer data.

Procurement thresholds (table):
| Action | Threshold | Required Steps |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Direct card purchase | <= $5k | Requester files receipt, local manager approves |
| Standard PO | $5k – $25k | Procurement issues PO, Finance validates budget |
| Formal RFQ / competitive | > $25k | Procurement runs competitive selection, legal review |
| Strategic vendor / contract | > $250k | Executive sponsorship, security & legal sign-off, board notification for strategic partnerships |

Vendor risk & security checks:
- Any vendor with access to customer or Redwood internal data must complete the security questionnaire and provide SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, or complete a security assessment by IT security.
- Vendors storing customer data in non-approved regions require Legal + Security exception.

5) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
Principles:
- Revenue must be recognized in accordance with ASC 606: identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, and recognize when obligations are satisfied.
- Redwood’s primary revenue streams: hosted API usage (consumption), Dedicated reserved capacity (contracted capacity), Private deployment licensing (term-based), and professional services (one-time or milestone-based).

Revenue treatment summary (table):
| Revenue Type | Performance Obligation | Recognition Trigger | Typical Billing Cadence | Deferred Revenue Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hosted API (consumption) | On-demand token processing | At time of usage (point-in-time) | Monthly invoice or post-pay auto-billing | N/A (recognized as used) |
| Dedicated (capacity commit) | Reserved capacity availability + committed usage credits | Recognize ratably over term as service is provided | Monthly or quarterly billing per contract | Recognize monthly; upfront prepayments recorded as deferred revenue and amortized over term |
| Private deployment license | License to deploy + support | Over time (if support/updates required) or point-in-time for perpetual license | Annual or upfront | Upfront payments amortized over support/term |
| Professional services | Implementation milestones | Upon completion of milestone / acceptance | Milestone billing / fixed fee | Recognize when milestone achieved; retainage per contract |

Billing and invoicing controls:
- Billing validation: Finance validates invoices against contract terms and usage reports; discrepancies > 2% require investigation.
- Invoice schedule: Standard invoices issued Net 30 unless customer agreement specifies alternative terms.
- Credit memos and SLA adjustments: Finance issues credit memos for validated SLA credits; all credits > $10k require CFO approval.
- Collections: Past-due invoices > 45 days routed to collections team and legal for remediation; sensitive or strategic customers escalated to Finance Director prior to collections.

Accounting system and metadata requirements:
- Every recognized contract must have a unique contract ID in the Finance system and be linked to CRM opportunity ID.
- Key contract metadata: contract start/end date, billing cadence, currency, tax treatment, GL codes, RevRec schedule ID.

6) Controls, Reporting, and Audit
- Monthly close: Finance runs revenue close within 7 business days of month-end with detail by revenue type and deferred revenue rollforward.
- Quarterly internal review: Legal + Finance review high-risk contracts, unusual billing terms, and large one-off credits.
- Audit readiness: Maintain source contracts, signed amendments, usage reports, and billing ledgers for 7 years. Coordinate with external auditors during annual audit; provide contract listing, RevRec schedules, and deferred revenue reconciliations.

7) Change Management and Exceptions
- Change requests to templates or thresholds: submit RFC to Finance Ops and Legal with rationale. Significant policy changes require CFO + GC approval.
- Exceptions: Documented exceptions (approved by Finance director + Legal) must be logged in the Exceptions register and reviewed quarterly.

Appendices:
A. Quick contract checklist (sales use):
1. Confirm template version.
2. Confirm pricing, billing cadence, and payment terms.
3. Identify data processing needs and attach DPA.
4. Route to Legal if any non-standard clause or indemnity requested.
5. Upload executed contract and key terms to repository.

B. Common GL codes and RevRec schedule IDs (examples):
- 4000: Hosted API Revenue (consumption) – REV-HOST
- 4010: Dedicated Reserved Capacity – REV-DEDI
- 4020: Private Deployment License – REV-LICENSE
- 4030: Professional Services – REV-PS

C. Change log:
- 2026-11-15: Initial published playbook (Daniela Romero).
- 2026-12-10: Added procurement thresholds and vendor security checklist (Marcus Li).
- 2027-01-10: Clarified RevRec treatment for Dedicated capacity and updated billing cadence (Priya Shah).
